meta.subtitle: Advanced Connectivity is growing and free cash flow is guided higher, but the price already reflects consensus and the EchoStar leverage step-up lies ahead

analystCommentary:
AT&T's second quarter of 2026 met the plan management set out early in the year. Growth in the Advanced Connectivity segment outran the decline of the copper-based Legacy business, free cash flow beat the company's own range for the quarter, and all consolidated full-year and multi-year guidance was reiterated alongside a larger 2026 buyback.

We rate the shares HOLD with a $25–$30 target range. Our scenarios value AT&T close to its current price of $26.53. The Base case applies a multiple just under today's current-year multiple to consensus FY27E earnings, the Bull pays a little more for a business guiding earnings and free cash flow higher through 2028, and the Bear prices a stall in earnings growth if satellite competition and convergence discounts bite. The valuation section sets out each anchor and shows that the label holds under a richer or a poorer Base.

The return case rests on income more than on price. What holds the multiple back is sequencing: net leverage rises after the EchoStar spectrum purchase before it falls, while dividends and buybacks are planned to absorb the guided free cash flow; convergence is diluting fiber ARPU; and the satellite question that moved the shares in July has no operating answer yet.

executiveSummary.companyOverview:
AT&T Inc. is a holding company, headquartered in Dallas, whose subsidiaries operate in the telecommunications and technology industries, mainly in the United States and, for wireless, in Mexico. Effective with its Q1 2026 reporting, the company realigned its segments into Advanced Connectivity (domestic 5G and fiber-based wireless, internet and other advanced connectivity services for consumer and business customers), Legacy (domestic legacy voice and data services over the copper-based network) and Latin America (wireless service and equipment in Mexico). Its stated goal is to power down and stop providing service over the large majority of its domestic copper-based network by the end of 2029. The United States produced 95.7% of FY25 revenue and Mexico 3.5%.

In the second quarter of 2026 Advanced Connectivity produced $28,615 million of segment operating revenues, Legacy $1,632 million and Latin America $1,224 million, against consolidated operating revenues of $31,558 million. The vendor's FY25 revenue mix uses six product labels that do not match these three segments; the moat section maps each label to the 10-Q and follows the 10-Q where they differ.

At June 30, 2026 the company had 109,800 thousand retail wireless subscribers, 74,921 thousand of them postpaid phones, and 15,479 thousand internet connections, 12,868 thousand of them fiber. On February 2, 2026 it closed its acquisition of substantially all of Lumen's Mass Markets fiber business. The acquired network assets sit in a wholly owned subsidiary, Forged Fiber, in which the company plans to sell a controlling interest to an equity partner, so they are reported as discontinued operations. On the July 22, 2026 call management said it expected its planned purchase of spectrum licenses from EchoStar to close by the end of July; the pack does not confirm the closing.

thesis.body:
AT&T is two businesses moving in opposite directions. Advanced Connectivity, which management told the call contributes over 90% of service revenue and nearly all of adjusted EBITDA, grew service revenue {+ +5.1% +} in the second quarter of 2026. Legacy revenue fell {- -25.9% -} as the company decommissions its copper-based network. The consolidated result is service revenue growth guided in the low-single-digit range.

Our view is that the plan is credible and largely priced. The quarter gave no sign that the mix shift is stalling, and the free cash flow guided for 2026 covers the dividend and the enlarged buyback. It leaves little room to reduce debt from retained cash while net leverage rises after the EchoStar purchase, and our weighted value sits close to the current price. We rate the shares HOLD: the income pays investors to wait, and a re-rating needs earnings ahead of consensus or evidence that satellite entrants are not raising churn.

catalysts: Closing of the EchoStar spectrum license purchase, which management expected by the end of July 2026, starts the deleveraging timetable set out in the balance-sheet section.
Free-cash-flow cadence in the second half: management expects a relatively stable third quarter and strong year-over-year growth in the fourth; the cash-flow section carries the reasons.
Fiber expansion toward the year-end footprint target, including the build-out of the acquired Lumen territories; the moat section carries the targets.
FCC copper-discontinuance approvals, which gate the Legacy exit; the risk section carries the progress and what a slower path would cost.
Sale of a controlling interest in Forged Fiber to an equity partner that would co-invest in the acquired Lumen network.
risks: Satellite competition: headlines tied a sharp fall in AT&T's shares in early July 2026 to SpaceX; the risk section sets out the churn measure to watch.
Fiber ARPU dilution from converged discounts; the risk section carries the cause and what would make it worse.
Net leverage rises after the EchoStar purchase while dividends and buybacks absorb the guided free cash flow; see the balance-sheet section.
Shrinking lines inside Advanced Connectivity: business transitional and other revenue and prepaid phone subscribers both fell year over year; the moat section carries the drivers.
Benefit-plan costs flow through reported earnings under the accounting election described in the February 2026 10-K.

financials.incomeCommentary:
FY25 revenue of $125.6B grew {+ +2.7% +} after FY22 {- -9.9% -}, FY23 +1.4% and FY24 -0.1%. Operating margin held in a narrow band, 20.2% in FY23, 19.8% in FY24 and 19.9% in FY25, while the vendor's gross margin moved from 43.7% in FY23 to 59.6% in FY25; with operating margin that steady, we do not read the gross-margin swing as an operating change and do not rely on it. The pack does not explain the FY22 operating loss (operating margin of -3.8%, diluted EPS of -$1.13). FY25 net income was $21.9B and diluted EPS $3.04; the valuation section explains why we use current-year rather than trailing earnings.

In the second quarter of 2026 consolidated operating revenues rose 2.3%, with service revenue up 2.7%. Total operating expenses rose only 0.7% because depreciation and amortization fell 5.4%, which the 10-Q attributes primarily to fully depreciated legacy assets. Operating income rose 8.3% to $7,038 million and the operating margin to 22.3% from 21.1%. Operations and support expense rose 2.4%, which the 10-Q attributes primarily to an asset abandonment charge tied to the reprioritization of its spectrum strategy, higher advertising, incremental customer costs from the acquired fiber business and higher bad debt from subscriber growth, partially offset by transformation savings, lower content licensing fees and gains on tower transactions.

Below operating income the quarter was weaker. Interest expense rose 13.8% to $1,883 million on higher debt balances and interest rates on long-term borrowings, and equity in net income of affiliates turned to a loss of $29 million from income of $485 million, primarily because of the sale of the DIRECTV interest to TPG Capital on July 2, 2025. Pre-tax income from continuing operations fell 4.5%. Income from continuing operations still rose 3.6% to $5,038 million because the effective tax rate fell to 13.5% from 20.3%, reflecting the resolution of certain IRS examinations. Diluted EPS from continuing operations was $0.66 versus $0.62; the release's adjusted EPS was $0.65 versus $0.54.
financials.balanceCommentary:
The vendor table shows total debt of $174.0B and net debt of $155.8B at December 31, 2025, while the release reports total debt of $144.0 billion and net debt of $126.4 billion at June 30, 2026. The two sets are six months apart and the pack does not reconcile them; we use the release's June figures because they match the quarter and are the basis management guides to. On that basis management put net debt to adjusted EBITDA at 2.68 times at quarter end, essentially flat with the prior quarter, close to the vendor's trailing 2.7x. Management expects the ratio to rise to the 3.2 times range after the EchoStar transaction closes and to return to a level consistent with its target in the 2.5x range within approximately three years of the closing. Every later reference in this report to the leverage step-up or the deleveraging window means this sequence.

Leverage of this order is part of how a capital-intensive network business is financed, and the measures that matter are coverage and the cash available after commitments. Trailing interest coverage is 3.6x. The constraint is timing rather than solvency: with dividends and buybacks planned to absorb the guided free cash flow, as the capital-allocation section sets out, we read the return to the target range as resting mainly on EBITDA growth rather than on debt paydown. Management said the company is well-positioned to fund the EchoStar transaction.

Cash and short-term investments were $18.2B at FY25 against $3.3B at FY24, and the current ratio was 0.91 against 0.66, with a trailing figure of 0.97. Total equity of $128.5B at FY25 compares with $183.9B at FY21; the step down came in FY22, and equity has risen each year since.
financials.cashflowCommentary:
Operating cash flow of $40.3B in FY25 funded capital expenditure of $20.8B and left free cash flow of $19.4B, a 15.5% margin. That is below the FY21 level of $25.4B but above FY23's $20.5B and FY24's $18.5B; the FY22 trough was $12.4B. FY25 repurchases of $6.6B compare with $0.2B in FY24, alongside $8.2B of dividends.

In the second quarter of 2026 cash from operating activities from continuing operations was $10.8 billion against $9.8 billion a year earlier. The release attributes the increase to lower cash tax payments and the timing of working capital payments, partially offset by a voluntary pension plan contribution of $100 million, and notes that the quarter benefited from $0.3 billion of cash received from DIRECTV, net of related tax payments. Capital expenditures rose to $5.7 billion from $4.9 billion, and capital investment, a non-GAAP measure, rose to $6.1 billion from $5.1 billion; management linked the increase to the faster pace of fiber deployment. Cash payments for vendor financing rose to $0.4 billion from $0.2 billion. Free cash flow of $4.7 billion against $4.4 billion exceeded the high end of the company's $4 billion-$4.5 billion range for the quarter.

For the full year management holds free cash flow at $18 billion+, and guides $19 billion+ for 2027 and $21 billion+ for 2028. It expects third-quarter free cash flow to be relatively stable year over year and the fourth quarter to show strong growth, because last year's fourth quarter was affected by discrete items including legal settlements and a large pension contribution.

valuation.multiplesCommentary:
At $26.53 the shares trade at 8.8x trailing earnings, 11.3x NTM earnings, about 10.4x FY27E EPS of $2.56, 6.1x trailing EV/EBITDA and 1.4x sales, with a 9.7% trailing free-cash-flow yield and a 4.18% dividend yield. The vendor's NTM multiple equals the price over FY26E consensus EPS of $2.34, so we treat the NTM multiple as the current-year multiple and use it as the like-for-like reference for every scenario: a year from now FY27 is the current year, so each scenario applies its multiple to FY27 earnings. The trailing multiple is not comparable, because FY25 diluted EPS of $3.04 sits well above the FY26E consensus. Peer multiples are pending a peer data source and the pack carries no history of the stock's own multiple, so the cross-checks are the company's guidance and the Street. Management guides adjusted EPS of $2.25 to $2.35 for 2026 with a double-digit three-year CAGR through 2028, and the FY26E consensus sits inside that range, near its top.

The Street sits close to the price. Of 62 analysts, 26 rate the shares Buy, 30 Hold and 6 Sell. The pack's consensus target equals the current price to the cent, so we do not treat it as an independent estimate; we use the median target of $27.50 and the $20.00–$30.00 range instead. The shares sit in the upper half of their 52-week range of $19.89–$29.79. The free-cash-flow yield is the bull's core argument for a business guiding free cash flow higher each year through 2028. The bear's is that the guided cash is committed to dividends and buybacks while net leverage rises, and that the satellite question set out in the risk section can move the multiple on headlines alone.

scenarios.name: Bull
scenarios.driver: Advanced Connectivity keeps growing service revenue at the 5%+ and EBITDA at the 6%+ guided for 2026, consensus FY27E EPS of $2.56 holds, and the double-digit adjusted EPS CAGR and $21 billion+ of free cash flow guided for 2028 look on track. The market pays 12x FY27E EPS, a whole-number multiple one step above today's current-year multiple and our judgment of what that 2028 path earns; $30.72 sits just above the top of the Street's $20.00–$30.00 target range.

scenarios.name: Base
scenarios.driver: Guidance is met as issued, the same FY27E consensus EPS holds, the $1.11 dividend is maintained and approximately $10 billion of buybacks are completed in 2026. The shares earn 11x FY27E EPS, a whole-number multiple just under today's 11.3x current-year multiple: the Street's median target of $27.50 sits below a full roll-forward of today's multiple, so we do not assume the market pays all of it. The Base value is $28.16.

scenarios.name: Bear
scenarios.driver: Satellite entrants and converged discounts lift postpaid phone churn from the second quarter's 0.86% and slow wireless service revenue growth, fiber ARPU keeps falling, and buybacks are scaled back to protect the dividend. Adjusted EPS lands at the $2.25 bottom of 2026 guidance and does not grow in 2027. With no earnings growth to price, the shares earn 9x, a whole-number multiple well below today's current-year multiple; $20.25 sits next to the bottom of the Street's target range and the 52-week low of $19.89.

valuation.scenarioCommentary:
Each driver applies a stated whole-number multiple to a stated EPS figure, so a reader can check it. The multiples rest on valuation evidence alone: the Bull's is our judgment of what the guided path to 2028 earns, the Base's reflects a Street median target below a full roll-forward of today's multiple, and the Bear's prices a stall in earnings growth, cross-checked against the bottom of the Street's range and the 52-week low. The Bear works through earnings and the multiple only; we do not deepen it for debt, because a price set on earnings is already after interest.

The weights rest on different evidence. The Base carries 55% because the second quarter met or beat the plan on service revenue, margins and free cash flow, and all consolidated guidance was reiterated. The Bull carries 20%, less than the Bear, because management's own timetable returns leverage to its target range only within approximately three years of the EchoStar closing, so a year out the ratio will still sit near its step-up. The Bear carries 25% because the July sell-off showed the market will re-price the shares on satellite headlines before any churn appears; postpaid phone churn fell in the quarter, which keeps it from carrying more.

The weighted fair value is $26.69 against the current price: expected upside E is +0.6%, bear-case downside D is -23.7% and reward/risk R is 0.03×, which derives HOLD. The label holds in both directions. Toward BUY, swapping the Bull and Bear weights, or rolling today's full current-year multiple onto FY27E EPS in the Base, still leaves E far below the +10.0% BUY needs; BUY needs a weighted value above even that roll-forward, which means earnings ahead of consensus. Toward SELL, moving the Base to the Street's median target leaves E just below zero, and SELL would need close to half the weight on the Bear. The $25–$30 target range brackets the Base and runs from below the weighted value to the top of the Street's range.

segments.name: Wireless Service
segments.body: The vendor's Wireless Service label, 55.8% of its FY25 mix, is closest to the wireless service line inside the 10-Q's Advanced Connectivity segment. Second-quarter 2026 wireless service revenue grew 3.3% year over year to $17,413 million, which the 10-Q attributes to growth in retail wireless subscribers in underpenetrated categories and converged accounts and to pricing actions, partially offset by promotional discounts on wireless subscriber additions. Postpaid phone net adds were 432,000 and postpaid phone churn was 0.86% against 0.87% a year earlier, while prepaid phone subscribers fell 3.4% to 16,518 thousand. Because it is more than half the mix, its growth rate carries the most weight in the moat judgment.

segments.name: Business Service
segments.body: The vendor's Business Service label has no single 10-Q counterpart. The closest lines are business fiber and advanced connectivity, which grew 10.0% to $1,946 million in the second quarter on higher fiber and fixed wireless revenues, and business transitional and other, which fell {- -16.6% -} to $1,042 million on lower demand for VPN and wholesale services, a decline the 10-Q expects to continue. The growth section carries management's outlook for business. Our read is that the business result is a mix outcome that improves only as the shrinking line becomes small enough to stop offsetting the growing one, which makes business a stabilizer for the moat rather than a source of it.

segments.name: Legacy Voice and Data
segments.body: The vendor's Legacy Voice and Data label is closest to the 10-Q's Legacy segment, domestic legacy voice and data services over the copper-based network. Second-quarter Legacy EBITDA fell {- -45.5% -} to $523 million and the margin to 32.0% from 43.6%, because revenue fell faster than direct operating costs, which were down 10.8%. Guidance has Legacy service revenue declining 20%+ in 2026 and immaterial by the end of 2029, and Legacy EBITDA is expected to turn negative after 2027 until the company has substantially eliminated the direct costs of its copper-based network. Legacy is a cost to be removed, not a franchise.

segments.name: IP Broadband
segments.body: The vendor's IP Broadband label ($3.5B in FY25) is closest to what the 10-Q now reports as advanced home internet; we cannot reconcile the two, so we use the 10-Q. Advanced home internet revenue grew {+ +27.3% +} in the second quarter to $2,926 million. Fiber revenues rose 21.4%, including customers of the acquired Lumen business, and AT&T Internet Air revenue increases exceeded 100%. Management expects revenue growth to continue as it invests further in building its fiber footprint. This line is the moat's growth edge; the risk section carries the ARPU cost of the convergence pricing behind it.

segments.name: Other Service
segments.body: The vendor's Other Service label matches the 10-Q's other service line, which fell 7.9% in the second quarter to $151 million on the continued decline in the number of consumer VoIP customers. It is immaterial to the thesis.

segments.name: Other Capitalized Property Plant and Equipment
segments.body: The vendor's Other Capitalized Property Plant and Equipment label, 19.5% of its FY25 mix, maps to no 10-Q revenue line, and the pack does not say what it contains, so we do not assign it to one. The 10-Q reports equipment revenue separately, at $5,581 million for the second quarter; it fell in Advanced Connectivity on lower hardware sales to business customers, offset by higher wireless device sales volumes. We set equipment aside when judging the moat.

moatFactors.name: Fiber footprint and convergence
moatFactors.body: Fiber reached 38.6 million consumer and business locations at the end of the second quarter, and management says it remains on track for over 40 million by the end of 2026 and more than 60 million by the end of 2030, with 8 million new locations planned this year, including over 4 million acquired from Lumen. Internet connections grew 29.5% year over year, and 42.5% of advanced home internet customers also have a postpaid wireless account, a convergence rate management ties to lower churn and higher lifetime values. The counter sits in the same disclosure: the rate reached 45% excluding the acquired Lumen footprint, so the acquired base is less converged than the rest.

moatFactors.name: Spectrum and network scale
moatFactors.body: Management told the call the company already has an advantaged low-band position and that what it called 'the 600' will make that advantage more substantial; the pack does not say what the 600 is, so we do not tie it to the EchoStar licenses. The scale behind it shows in a postpaid phone base that grew 2.1% year over year while postpaid phone churn edged lower. The counter is that spectrum is bought rather than built, and buying it drives the leverage step-up the balance-sheet section sets out.

moatFactors.name: Switching costs from bundling
moatFactors.body: Headlines on June 30, 2026 reported that AT&T expanded Build-A-Plan so customers can add fiber or AT&T Internet Air to a customizable wireless plan. Management says converged customers typically stay longer and increase their spending over time, and it also says they enjoy discounted pricing. Switching costs exist, but they are bought with discounts; the risk section carries the ARPU cost.

moatFactors.name: Operating leverage and cost position
moatFactors.body: Advanced Connectivity operating income rose {+ +20.3% +} to $7,345 million in the second quarter on segment revenue up 4.1%, lifting the segment operating margin to 25.7% from 22.2% and the EBITDA margin to 42.0% from 40.5%. The release credits lower depreciation from fully depreciated legacy assets, transformation savings, lower content licensing fees and tower transaction gains. Management says it remains on pace for $4 billion in consolidated annual cost savings by the end of 2028, and the consolidated adjusted EBITDA margin reached 39.1%. The counter is that part of the gain came from tower gains and depreciation relief rather than from pricing.

businessMoat.durability: We rate the moat narrow. The evidence for pricing power is mixed: the 10-Q credits wireless service growth to pricing actions net of promotional discounts and calls the effective management of churn critical to revenue growth and margins, which describes a market where share is contested. The July sell-off, set out in the risk section, shows the market can re-price the franchise on a satellite headline. What is durable is the fiber footprint: locations passed cannot be replicated quickly, and the build is accelerating, as the fiber factor above sets out. Latin America grew segment revenues 16.1% in the quarter on favorable foreign exchange rates and postpaid wireless subscriber growth, but it adds nothing to the moat. The moat widens if the convergence rate keeps rising and narrows if satellite entrants reset wireless pricing; the Legacy exit removes a drag on returns rather than adding protection.

points: Advanced Connectivity is guided to mid-single-digit service revenue growth annually through 2028, including 5%+ in 2026, with segment EBITDA growth in the mid-to-high-single-digit range and 6%+ in 2026; management said second-quarter service revenue growth accelerated by 150 basis points from Q1.

Home internet carries the growth: internet net adds were 646,000 in the quarter, 367,000 fiber and 279,000 fixed wireless, and AT&T Internet Air connections rose 93.9% to 1,951 thousand. Net adds exclude acquisition-related activity, while advanced home internet revenue includes the acquired Lumen customers.

Wireless growth is coming from new accounts as well as lines: management said the 147,000 consumer postpaid wireless accounts added in the quarter were its best result in more than three years, and that postpaid phone ARPU grew year over year while postpaid phone churn fell.

Business Advanced Connectivity service revenues grew 1.8% in the quarter on wireless, fiber and fixed wireless, and management expects them to grow at a low single-digit CAGR through 2028; the shrinking business transitional line will keep subtracting, as the moat section sets out.

Consolidated growth stays low while Legacy shrinks: management guides adjusted EBITDA growth in the 3% to 4% range in 2026, improving to 5% or better in 2028. Consensus has FY26E revenue of ~$129.2B and FY27E of $131.9B.

management.leadership: John Stankey is Chairman and CEO, as the July 2026 release identifies him, so one person leads both the board and management; the proxy excerpt does not say how the board balances that. The March 2026 proxy states that the Corporate Governance Guidelines require a substantial majority of independent directors, lists the directors the Board determined to be independent, and states that every member of the Audit, Governance and Policy, and Human Resources Committees is independent; the excerpt gives no board size, so the ratio cannot be checked here. Operationally the team delivered the quarter it guided to and reiterated all consolidated guidance, and the segment realignment provides, in the 10-Q's words, better visibility into the progress of exiting the copper-based legacy operations. We discount one part of the call: the agentic-AI traffic figures (up to 450% more total traffic per task, and approximately 9X enterprise and 7X consumer traffic growth by 2035) are industry research management cited, not a company forecast, and we do not value the shares on them.
management.capitalAllocation: The framework for 2026–2028 is explicit: capital investment in the $23 billion to $24 billion range annually, the annualized common dividend held at $1.11 per share, approximately $24 billion of share repurchases with approximately $10 billion in 2026, and $45 billion+ returned to shareholders over the three years. The 2026 buyback compares with a prior target of $8 billion and, management said, pulls forward planned buybacks through 2028 to capture what it sees as a disparity between the company's operating fundamentals and the valuation of its stock. Planned repurchases and expected dividends total approximately $18 billion this year, which management called essentially all of its free-cash-flow outlook. Second-quarter returns were $4.1 billion, including approximately $2.2 billion of repurchases, and management said it was on pace to buy back nearly $1 billion of stock in July. Two judgments sit inside this. The EchoStar spectrum purchase comes at the same time as the faster buyback, so the balance sheet absorbs the timing. The Lumen fiber deal is structured so that a controlling interest in the acquired network is to be sold to an equity partner, which would bring outside capital into the build if the sale closes.
management.governance: The March 2026 proxy shows compensation set by a Human Resources Committee composed entirely of independent directors, and say-on-pay support of 90.7% of votes cast at the 2025 Annual Meeting. The 2025 short-term plan paid a 112% weighted average: compensation-adjusted operating income, at a 60% weight, attained 104% and paid 118%; free cash flow, at a 20% weight, attained 100% and paid 101%; and the strategic component, also at 20%, shows no attainment figure and paid 105%, so a fifth of the bonus paid above target on a measure the proxy table does not score. In the 2023–2025 long-term plan a three-year compensation-adjusted EPS CAGR of 0.6% earned a 128% payout on its half, which implies a target set below that growth rate, while the relative TSR modifier was 0% for a third-quartile ranking. Related-person transactions need Governance and Policy Committee approval under a written policy, and the excerpt records an approved employment of a related person but is cut off before naming the person. The Board tested two relationships for independence: the company where Ms. Taylor is an executive officer bought communications services from AT&T subsidiaries in 2025, with payments below 1% of each company's consolidated gross revenues against the NYSE's 2% limit, and Mr. Kennard has a less than 5% equity interest in an investment manager that invests in a company transacting with AT&T. The Board found both independent.
management.insiderOwnership: The March 2026 proxy excerpt in our pack does not include the beneficial ownership table, so we do not quantify director or executive holdings and make no claim about insider buying or selling. What the excerpt does show is the mechanism meant to align pay with holders: at-risk target compensation for each named executive officer tied to stock price and predetermined goals, and a related-person policy with a $120,000 disclosure threshold administered by the Governance and Policy Committee.

idiosyncratic: Satellite competition. Morningstar headlines on July 2, 2026 said AT&T was on pace for its worst week since March 2020 and called the sell-off a SpaceX panic. No operating figure in the quarter shows satellite taking share, the transcript excerpt does not discuss satellite, and postpaid phone churn was lower year over year. The episode shows the multiple can move on satellite headlines before any churn appears. The measure to watch is postpaid phone churn against the second-quarter level set out in the moat section.

Leverage around the EchoStar purchase. Interest expense is already rising on higher debt balances and rates, and net leverage is guided up before it comes down, as the balance-sheet section sets out. A slip in Advanced Connectivity EBITDA growth during that window would force a choice between the buyback pace and the deleveraging timetable.

Fiber ARPU and the price of convergence. Management said fiber ARPU fell 1.3% year over year, primarily reflecting the lower-ARPU subscribers acquired from Lumen, and was approximately flat excluding them; it expects its focus on convergence to put some pressure on fiber ARPU in the near term. Advanced home internet growth therefore depends on volume. If fiber net adds slow while ARPU is still falling, that line would slow faster than the subscriber count suggests.

Legacy exit economics. The exit depends on regulators: the company has approval to discontinue legacy services in over 30% of its wire centers, effective by late 2026, and the FCC permitted it to discontinue legacy copper voice service at about 60% of its California wire centers. Because Legacy EBITDA is guided to turn negative after 2027, as the moat section sets out, a slower regulatory path or slower customer migration would leave copper cost in the income statement for longer.

Benefit plans and the income statement. The February 2026 10-K notes that the company reflects annual funded-status adjustments to its pension and postretirement plans in the consolidated statement of income, so lower asset returns, higher medical costs or rate moves flow through reported earnings; the voluntary $100 million pension contribution in the quarter shows that funding needs cash too.
risks.systemic: The February 2026 10-K leads its risk factors with macro-economic exposures: a higher interest rate environment, inflation and medical costs that could raise benefit plan costs; inflationary and supply pressure on devices and network components, including pressure on semiconductors as hyperscalers and others spend to support AI; and capital-market access, where credit-rating downgrades could raise borrowing costs and require collateral under derivative agreements, which matters more while leverage rises. Industry-wide, changes to federal, state and foreign regulation and private litigation could raise operating costs, and FCC copper-discontinuance rulings can speed or slow the Legacy exit. Mexico adds currency and political exposure. The 10-K also warns that higher prices may raise churn and that, under inflationary pressure or a downturn, consumers may buy lower-priced offerings or forgo purchases, the same churn and ARPU tension that runs through this report.

body: **HOLD, target range $25–$30.** AT&T is executing its plan, and the quarter gave no sign that the shift from copper to fiber and 5G is stalling. At 11.3x current-year consensus EPS the price already reflects most of what consensus expects: our weighted fair value of $26.69 gives expected upside of +0.6%, against a Bear case 23.7% below the price.

The label rests on what the page shows. The 2026 free cash flow guidance is committed to dividends and buybacks while net leverage rises after the EchoStar purchase, convergence is diluting fiber ARPU, and the satellite question has moved the shares without yet showing up in churn. The dividend pays investors to wait.

On unchanged scenarios, a close at the Base value of $28.16 would derive SELL, and BUY would need the price to fall to where the weighted value sits 10.0% above it, below our target low. We would lift the Base above a roll-forward of today's multiple, the step BUY needs, only on earnings running ahead of the $2.56 FY27E consensus. We would add weight to the Bear on a rise in postpaid phone churn or a cut to 2026 guidance, though SELL needs close to half the weight there.
